metadata.source: Śrī Kedāra Nātha Śarmā: Vṛttaratnākara : with a commentary of Bhaṭṭa Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭ and notes etc. by Vaidya Nātha Śāstrī Varakale, edited with the Maṇimayī Hindī Commentary. -- 6th ed. Varanasi : Chaukhambha Sanskrit Sansthan , 1980. (The Kashi Sanskrit Series ; 55)

children.translated_text: [Auspiciousness]
[<s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> (Ocean of Metres)]
Chapter One
For the attainment of an unbroken succession of happiness, having bowed to <s>Brahmā</s> and worshipped <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),
I salute <s>Śaṅkara</s>, accompanied by <s>Gaurī</s> and <s>Vināyaka</s>, who brings welfare to the world. // KedV_1.1 //
There was one learned in the meaning of the <s>Vedas</s> and the <s>Śaiva</s> scriptures, named <s>Pavya</s> (?), [devoted to] the welfare of the world.

children.text: tasya putro 'sti kedāraḥ śivapādārcane rataḥ // KedV_1.2 //
children.translated_text: His son is <s>Kedāra</s>, devoted to the worship of the feet of <s>Śiva</s>. // KedV_1.2 //
By him is composed this work on metre, furnished with both examples and definitions,
named <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> (Ocean of Metres), for the easy understanding of beginners. // KedV_1.3 //
That which was stated as twofold — secular metre — by <s>Piṅgala</s> and other earlier teachers,
distinguished by <s>mātrā</s> (mora) and <s>varṇa</s> (syllable), that <s>chandas</s> (metre) is described here. // KedV_1.4 //
Of this metrical treatise, composed in six chapters, the clearly established
measure should be known as one hundred and thirty-six [metres]. // KedV_1.5 //
By these ten syllabic patterns — <s>ma</s>, <s>ya</s>, <s>ra</s>, <s>sa</s>, <s>ta</s>, <s>ja</s>, <s>bha</s>, <s>na</s>, <s>ga</s>, <s>la</s> —

children.text: samastaṃ vāṅmayaṃ vyāptaṃ trailokyamiva viṣṇunā // KedV_1.6 //
children.translated_text: the entire domain of speech is pervaded, just as the three worlds are pervaded by <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // KedV_1.6 //
<s>Ma</s> has all heavy syllables; ending with light syllables from the beginning are <s>ya</s> and <s>ra</s>; with light syllables at the end and beginning are <s>sa</s> and <s>ta</s>;

children.text: gmadhyādyau jmau trilo no 'ṣṭau bhavantyatra gaṇāstrikāḥ // KedV_1.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ga</s> has a heavy middle; the initial and middle are for <s>ja</s> and <s>ma</s>; with three lights is <s>na</s>. Thus eight <s>gaṇas</s> (metrical groups) are trisyllabic. // KedV_1.7 //
Those with a heavy syllable at the end, middle, and beginning respectively should be known as four-mora
<s>gaṇas</s>; and those with four light syllables are found in <s>āryā</s> and similar metres. // KedV_1.8 //
A syllable followed by <s>anusvāra</s>, ending in <s>visarga</s>, long by nature, or followed by a conjunct consonant,

children.text: vā pādānte tvasau gvakro jñeyo 'nyo mātriko lṛjuḥ // KedV_1.9 //
children.translated_text: or optionally at the end of a <s>pāda</s> (quarter-verse) — that is known as <s>guru</s> (heavy); any other is <s>laghu</s> (light), with one <s>mātrā</s>. // KedV_1.9 //
Here, a conjunct at the beginning of a <s>pāda</s> is called <s>krama</s> (initial conjunction).

children.text: puraḥsthitena tena syāllaghutā 'pi kvacid guroḥ // KedV_1.10 //
children.translated_text: By its preceding syllable, even a heavy syllable may sometimes become light. // KedV_1.10 //

children.text: taruṇaṃ sarṣapaśākaṃ navaudanaṃ picchilāni ca dadhīni /
children.translated_text: Fresh mustard greens, newly cooked rice, and slimy curds —
O beautiful one, the village folk enjoy delicious [food] at little expense. // KedV_1.11 //
The technical designations of oceans, elements, sentiments, and so forth should be known from common usage.
A <s>pāda</s> (foot) should be known as a quarter; <s>yati</s> (caesura) is designated as a pause. // KedV_1.12 //
The even and uneven positions in a verse are stated by the learned as follows:

children.text: samamardhasamaṃ vṛttaṃ viṣamaṃ ca tathāparam // KedV_1.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sama</s> (uniform), <s>ardhasama</s> (half-uniform), and <s>viṣama</s> (non-uniform) — thus are the three types of <s>vṛtta</s> (metre). // KedV_1.13 //
That metre whose four feet are marked by identical characteristics
is called <s>sama vṛtta</s> (uniform metre) by those who know the essence of the science of prosody. // KedV_1.14 //
That metre in which the first foot is the same as the third,
and the second is like the fourth, is called <s>ardhasama</s> (half-uniform). // KedV_1.15 //
That metre in which the characteristics of the four feet
are mutually different is called <s>viṣama vṛtta</s> (non-uniform metre) by those skilled in the science of prosody. // KedV_1.16 //
Beginning from a foot of one syllable, increasing by one syllable each,
a separate metre exists for each foot-length up to twenty-six syllables. // KedV_1.17 //
Beyond that, <s>Caṇḍavṛṣṭi</s> and other <s>daṇḍakas</s> (extended metres) are proclaimed.
The rest are <s>gāthās</s>, characterized by three or six feet. // KedV_1.18 //
<s>Ukta</s>, <s>Atyukta</s>, then <s>Madhyā</s>, <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>, next <s>Supūrvikā</s>,

children.text: gāyatryuṣṇiganuṣṭup ca bṛhatī paṅktireva ca // KedV_1.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Uṣṇik</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, <s>Bṛhatī</s>, and <s>Paṅkti</s>, // KedV_1.19 //

children.text: triṣṭup ca jagatī caiva tathā 'tijagatī matā /
children.translated_text: <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Jagatī</s>, and likewise <s>Atijagatī</s>,

children.text: śakvarī sā 'tipūrvā syādaṣṭyatyaṣṭī tataḥ smṛte // KedV_1.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakvarī</s>, then <s>Atipūrvā</s>, <s>Aṣṭi</s>, and <s>Atyaṣṭi</s> are thus declared. // KedV_1.20 //
<s>Dhṛti</s> and <s>Atidhṛti</s>, <s>Kṛti</s>, <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Ākṛti</s>,
<s>Vikṛti</s>, <s>Saṅkṛti</s>, and likewise <s>Atikṛti</s> and <s>Utkṛti</s>. // KedV_1.21 //
Thus have the designations of the metres been stated. I shall now describe in order
the definitions of all metres, beginning with the <s>mātrā</s>-based metres. // KedV_1.22 //

children.text: iti śrīkedārabhaṭṭaviracite vṛttaratnākare saṃjñābhidhāno nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, entitled 'On Designations,' in the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> composed by <s>Śrī Kedārabhaṭṭa</s>.
Chapter Two
[Section on <s>Āryā</s> metre (1-7)]

children.text: lakṣmaitatsapta gaṇā gopetā bhavati neha viṣame jaḥ /
children.translated_text: Its characteristic is this: seven <s>gaṇas</s> followed by <s>ga</s> (a heavy syllable); in the odd feet <s>ja</s>-gaṇa does not occur.

children.text: ṣaṣṭho 'yaṃ nalaghū vā prathame 'rdhe niyatamāryāyāḥ // KedV_2.1 //
children.translated_text: The sixth [gaṇa] must be either of one light syllable or [not light]; in the first half [of the <s>Āryā</s>] these rules are fixed. // KedV_2.1 //
In the sixth [gaṇa], after the <s>la</s> (light syllable) of the second [half], with <s>na</s> and <s>la</s> from the initial <s>la</s>, and with the rule of <s>yati</s> (caesura) at the foot,

children.text: carame 'rdhe pañcake tasmādiha bhavati ṣaṣṭho laḥ // KedV_2.2 //
children.translated_text: in the latter half, in the fifth [gaṇa], therefore the sixth here is <s>la</s> (light). // KedV_2.2 //
She whose foot appears at three odd positions in the two halves

children.text: pathyeti nāma tasyāḥ prakīrtitaṃ nāgarājena // KedV_2.3 //
children.translated_text: is named <s>Pathyā</s>, as declared by <s>Nāgarāja</s> (<s>Piṅgala</s>). // KedV_2.3 //
is called <s>Vipulā</s> (extended) by <s>Piṅgala Nāga</s>. // KedV_2.4 //
She in whose two halves the foot occurs by skipping the first three <s>gaṇas</s>
She in whose both halves <s>ja</s>-gaṇas are the second and fourth, with <s>ga</s> (heavy) in the middle,

children.text: capaleti nāma tasyā prakīrtitaṃ nāgarājena // KedV_2.5 //
children.translated_text: is named <s>Capalā</s> (fickle), as declared by <s>Nāgarāja</s>. // KedV_2.5 //

children.text: ādyaṃ dalaṃ samastaṃ bhajeya lakṣma capalāgataṃ yasyāḥ /
children.translated_text: She whose first half entirely follows the characteristics of <s>Capalā</s>,
while the remainder has the <s>ja</s>-characteristic of the earlier [type], is called <s>Mukhacapalā</s> by the sage. // KedV_2.6 //
She in whose first half the previously described [characteristic appears], and in the latter half that of <s>Capalā</s>,
is called <s>Jaghanacapalā</s> by those of pure intellect. // KedV_2.7 //
[Section on <s>Gīti</s> metre (8-11)]
If whatever characteristics described for the first half of the <s>Āryā</s> are found

children.text: dalayoḥ krṭayatiśobhāṃ tāṃ gītiṃ gītavānbhujaṅgeśaḥ // KedV_2.8 //
children.translated_text: in both halves, producing the beauty of equal <s>yati</s> — that <s>Gīti</s> was sung by <s>Bhujaṅgeśa</s> (<s>Piṅgala</s>). // KedV_2.8 //
If the characteristics stated for the second half of the <s>Āryā</s>
are found in both halves — that is called <s>Upagīti</s> by the sage. // KedV_2.9 //
She whose two halves of the <s>Āryā</s> are arranged in reverse order
is called <s>Udgīti</s>; likewise, that which has the distinction of reversed parts [is the same]. // KedV_2.10 //
If the first half of the <s>Āryā</s> is furnished with one extra heavy syllable at the end,
and the other [half] is likewise complete — that is called <s>Āryāgīti</s>. // KedV_2.11 //
[Section on <s>Vaitālīya</s> metre (12-20)]

children.text: ṣaḍviṣame 'ṣṭau same kalāstāśca same syurno nirantarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Six <s>mātrās</s> in the odd [feet], eight in the even [feet]; and those in the even [feet] are not consecutive.

children.text: na samātra parāśritā kalā vaitālīye 'nte ralā guruḥ // KedV_2.12 //
children.translated_text: No <s>mātrā</s> here depends on the following one; in the <s>Vaitālīya</s>, the ending is <s>ra</s>, <s>la</s>, and <s>guru</s> (heavy). // KedV_2.12 //

children.text: paryante ryau tathaiva śeṣamaupacchandasikaṃ sudhībhiruktam // KedV_2.13 //
children.translated_text: At the end [are] <s>ra</s> and <s>ya</s>; the rest is as before — that is called <s>Aupacchandasika</s> by the learned. // KedV_2.13 //
This is called <s>Āpātalikā</s>: [when the ending is] <s>bha</s> followed by <s>guru</s>; the rest is as before. // KedV_2.14 //
<s>Dakṣiṇāntikā</s>: with the third [and fourth feet] paired, in all feet the second is <s>la</s> (light). // KedV_2.15 //
<s>Udīcyavṛtti</s>: the second is <s>la</s> (light), joined with the following [syllable] in the odd [feet]. // KedV_2.16 //

children.text: pūrveṇa yuto 'tha pañcamaḥ prācyavṛttiruditeti yugmayoḥ // KedV_2.17 //
children.translated_text: The fifth joined with the preceding [syllable] in the even [feet] — that is called <s>Prācyavṛtti</s>. // KedV_2.17 //
When the even [feet] follow the pattern of the odd pair of the first [type], that is called <s>Pravṛttaka</s>. // KedV_2.18 //
Its even-footed counterpart is <s>Aparāntikā</s>. // KedV_2.19 //
The odd-footed [variant] is <s>Cāruhāsinī</s>. // KedV_2.20 //
[Section on <s>Vaktra</s> metre (21-30)]
<s>Vaktra</s>: the even feet have <s>na</s> and <s>sa</s> — it is known by the name <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> from the ocean [of metres]. // KedV_2.21 //
In the even [feet], with <s>ja</s>-gaṇa from the river's lord — that is called <s>Pathyāvaktra</s>. // KedV_2.22 //
In the odd [feet], with <s>ja</s>-gaṇa from the ocean — that itself is called <s>Viparītādi</s> (reversed). // KedV_2.23 //
<s>Capalāvaktra</s>: in the odd [feet], with <s>na</s>-gaṇa from the ocean. // KedV_2.24 //

children.text: yasyā laḥ saptamo yugme sā yugmavipulā matā // KedV_2.25 //
children.translated_text: She whose seventh [syllable] in the even [feet] is <s>la</s> (light) — that is regarded as <s>Yugmavipulā</s>. // KedV_2.25 //
The same applies to all of its [variants]. // KedV_2.26 //
With <s>bha</s>-gaṇa from the ocean — that is <s>Bhavipulā</s>. // KedV_2.27 //
Likewise another, with <s>ra</s> after the fourth [position]. // KedV_2.28 //
With <s>na</s>-gaṇa from the ocean — that is <s>Navipulā</s>. // KedV_2.29 //
With <s>ta</s>-gaṇa from the ocean — and its preceding variant is another. // KedV_2.30 //
[Section on <s>Mātrāsamaka</s> metre (31-38)]
Twice eight light syllables, [then] mountain-steadfast — thus. // KedV_2.31 //
<s>Mātrāsamaka</s>: the ninth is ending in <s>la</s> and <s>ga</s>. // KedV_2.32 //
<s>Ja</s>-gaṇa [and] <s>na</s>, <s>la</s> — from the ocean: that is <s>Viśloka</s>. // KedV_2.33 //
From a pair of those [comes] <s>Vānavāsikā</s>. // KedV_2.34 //
If in the arrows [= 5th], eighth, and ninth [positions], <s>la</s> (light) is placed — that is <s>Citā</s>. // KedV_2.35 //
<s>Upacitrā</s>: the ninth is joined with the following. // KedV_2.36 //
That which is composed with feet following the characteristics of <s>Mātrāsamaka</s> and the various [metres] described above,
with an unrestricted number of feet in each verse — that is known in the world as <s>Pādākulaka</s>. // KedV_2.37 //

children.text: vṛttasya lā vinā varṇairgā varṇā gurubhistathā /
children.translated_text: The measure of a verse-half is fixed as follows: lights in place of heavy syllables, heavy syllables in place of lights,

children.text: guruvo lairdale nityaṃ pramāṇamiti niścitam // KedV_2.38 //
children.translated_text: and heavy syllables [counted as] lights in the half — this is the definite standard. // KedV_2.38 //
Peacock-multiplied ten lights, composed [thus], with the removal of pairs of lights, and the rest entirely

children.text: saguru śakalayugalakamapi suparighaṭitalalitapadavitati bhavati śikhā // KedV_2.39 //
children.translated_text: ending with a heavy syllable in both halves — [this] well-constructed, elegant sequence of words constitutes <s>Śikhā</s>. // KedV_2.39 //
With interchanged halves composed of an elegant sequence of words, constituting a collection of virtues,

children.text: śrutisukhakṛdiyamapi jagati ñi jaśira upagatavati sati bhavati khajā // KedV_2.40 //
children.translated_text: this [metre], pleasing to the ear, occurs in the world when <s>na</s>, <s>ja</s>, <s>śa</s>, and <s>ra</s> are present — it becomes <s>Khajā</s>. // KedV_2.40 //
She whose halves have eight heavy syllables, each doubled — that is called <s>Anaṅgakrīḍā</s>.

children.text: dalamaparamapi vasuguṇitasalilanidhilaghu kaviracitaṃ padavitati bhavati // KedV_2.41 //
mo mo go go vidyunmālā // KedV_3.13 //
syādindravajrā yadi tau jagau gaḥ // KedV_3.28 //
vātormīyaṃ kathitā mbhau tagau gaḥ // KedV_3.35 //
mbhau nlau gaḥ syād bhramaravilasitam // KedV_3.37 //
tyau tyau maṇimālā cchinnā guhavaktraiḥ // KedV_3.58 //
( upasthitamidaṃ jsau tsau sagurukaṃ cet ) // KedV_3.73 //
uktā vasantatilakā tabhajā jagau gaḥ // KedV_3.79 //
dviḥsaptacchidalolā msau mbhau gau caraṇe cet // KedV_3.83 //
bhavati najau bhajau rasahitau prabhadrakam // KedV_3.88 //
mrau myau yāntau bhavetāṃ saptāṣṭabhiścandralekhā // KedV_3.90 //
najabhajaraiḥ sadā bhavati vāṇinī gayuktaiḥ // KedV_3.92 //
rasai rudraiśchinnā yamanasabhalā gaḥ śikhariṇī // KedV_3.93 //
jasau jasayalā vasugrahayatiśca pṛthvī guruḥ // KedV_3.94 //
rasayugahayairnsau mrau slau gau yadā hariṇī tadā // KedV_3.96 //
mandākrāntā jaladhiṣaḍagairmbhaunatau tād guru cet // KedV_3.97 //
syād bhūtartvaśvaiḥ kusumitalatāvellitā mtau nayau yau // KedV_3.100 //
jñeyā saptāśvaṣaḍbhrmarabhanayayutā bhlo gaḥ suvadanā // KedV_3.102 //
trī rajau galau bhavedihedṛśena lakṣaṇena vṛttanāma // KedV_3.103 //
mrabhnairyānāṃ trayeṇa trimuniyatiyutā sragdharā kīrtiteyam // KedV_3.104 //
bhrau naranā ranāvatha gururdigarkaviramaṃ hi bhadrakamiti // KedV_3.105 //
yadiha najau bhajau bhjabhalagāstadaśvalalitaṃ harārkayatimam // KedV_3.106 //
matākrīḍā mau tnau nau nalgiti bhavati vasuśaradaśayatiyutā // KedV_3.107 //
bhūtamuninairyatiriha bhatanāḥ sbhau bhanayāśca yadi bhavati tanvī // KedV_3.108 //
krauñjapadā bhamau smau nananā ngāviṣaśaravasumuniviratiriha bhavet // KedV_3.109 //
mo nāḥ ṣaṭ sagagiti yadi navarasarasaśarayatiyutamapavāhākhyam // KedV_3.111 //
yadi ha nayugalaṃ tataḥ saptarephā stadā caṇḍavṛṣṭiprapāto bhaveddaṇḍakaḥ // KedV_3.112 //
pracitakasamabhidho dhīradhībhiḥ smṛtodaṇḍako nadvayāduttaraiḥ saptabhiryaiḥ // KedV_3.114 //
children.translated_text: That [meter] called <s>pracitaka</s> is recognized by the learned as an [eleven-syllable] <s>udaṇḍaka</s> composed of <s>na</s>-<s>na</s> [gaṇas] followed by seven [syllables] after the first two [gaṇas]. // KedV_3.114 //
Thus ends the third chapter on <s>samavṛtta</s> (equal meters) in the commentary on the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> composed by <s>Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa</s>, son of the illustrious <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmeśvara</s>.
Chapter Four.

children.text: viṣame yadi sau salagā dale bhau yuji bhād gurukāvupacitram // KedV_4.1 //
children.translated_text: In the odd [quarters], if [there are] <s>sa</s>, <s>la</s> (light syllable), and <s>ga</s> (heavy syllable), and in the even [quarters] <s>bha</s> and <s>u</s> (light syllable); in the even [quarter after] <s>bha</s>, two heavy syllables — [this meter is called] <s>upacitra</s>. // KedV_4.1 //

children.text: bhatrayamojagataṃ guruṇī cedyuji ca najau jyayutā drutamadhyā // KedV_4.2 //
children.translated_text: Three <s>bha</s>-gaṇas in the odd [quarters] with a heavy [syllable] at the end; and in the even [quarters] <s>na</s>-<s>ja</s> [gaṇas] with <s>ya</s> added — [this is] <s>drutamadhyā</s>. // KedV_4.2 //

children.text: sayugātsagurū viṣame cedbhāviha vegavatī yuji bhādgau // KedV_4.3 //
children.translated_text: After [the first] <s>sa</s>-group, [if there are] <s>sa</s> and two heavy [syllables] in the odd [quarters]; and <s>bha</s> here [followed by a heavy syllable] — [this is] <s>vegavatī</s>; in the even [quarter], after <s>bha</s>, two heavy [syllables]. // KedV_4.3 //

children.text: oje taparau jarau guruścenmasau jgaugbhadravirāṅ bhavedanoje // KedV_4.4 //
children.translated_text: In the odd [quarters], <s>ta</s>-<s>pa</s> (i.e. <s>ta</s>-<s>ra</s>), <s>ja</s>-<s>ra</s>, and a heavy syllable; and in the non-odd (i.e. even) [quarters], <s>ma</s>-<s>sa</s>, <s>ja</s>-<s>ga</s>-<s>u</s>-<s>ga</s> — this would be <s>bhadravirāṭ</s>. // KedV_4.4 //

children.text: asame sajo saguruyuktau ketumatī same bharanagādgaḥ // KedV_4.5 //
children.translated_text: In the unequal [quarters], <s>sa</s>-<s>ja</s> with <s>sa</s> and a heavy [syllable] added — [this is] <s>ketumatī</s>; in the equal [quarters], <s>bha</s>-<s>ra</s>-<s>na</s>-<s>ga</s> followed by a heavy [syllable]. // KedV_4.5 //

children.text: ākhyānakīṃ tau jagurū ga oje jatāvanoje jagurū guruścet // KedV_4.6 //
children.translated_text: [The meter is called] <s>ākhyānakī</s>: <s>ta</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ja</s> and two heavy [syllables], and <s>ga</s> in the odd [quarter]; <s>ja</s>-<s>ta</s>-<s>va</s> in the non-odd [quarter]; <s>ja</s> and two heavy [syllables] with a heavy at the end. // KedV_4.6 //

children.text: jatau jagau go viṣame same cettau jgau ga eṣā viparītapūrvā // KedV_4.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ja</s>-<s>ta</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ja</s>-<s>ga</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>go</s> in the odd [quarter]; and in the even [quarter] <s>ta</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ja</s>-<s>ga</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ga</s> — this is [<s>ākhyānakī</s>] <s>viparītapūrvā</s> (with reversed first [quarter]). // KedV_4.7 //

children.text: sayugātsalaghū viṣame gururyuji nabhau bharakau hariṇaplutā // KedV_4.8 //
children.translated_text: After [the first] <s>sa</s>-group, <s>sa</s> and two light [syllables] in the odd [quarter], [then] a heavy; in the even [quarter] <s>na</s>-<s>bha</s> and <s>bha</s>-<s>ra</s>, two heavy — [this is] <s>hariṇaplutā</s>. // KedV_4.8 //

children.text: ayuji nanaralā guruḥ samenjamaparavaktramidaṃ tato jarau // KedV_4.9 //
children.translated_text: In the odd [quarter] <s>na</s>-<s>na</s>-<s>ra</s>-<s>la</s> and a heavy [syllable]; in the even [quarter] <s>ja</s>-<s>ma</s> — this is <s>aparavaktra</s>; thereafter <s>ja</s>-<s>ra</s> and <s>u</s>. // KedV_4.9 //

children.text: ayuji nayugarephato yakāro yuji ca najau jaragāśca puṣpitāgrā // KedV_4.10 //
children.translated_text: In the odd [quarter] <s>na</s>-group, <s>ra</s>, and then <s>ya</s>; and in the even [quarter] <s>na</s>-<s>ja</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ja</s>-<s>ra</s>, and <s>ga</s> [gaṇas] — [this is] <s>puṣpitāgrā</s>. // KedV_4.10 //
The learned call [the meter] known as <s>aparavaktra</s> also <s>vaitālīya</s>;
And some call <s>puṣpitāgrā</s> also <s>aupacchandasika</s>. // KedV_4.11 //

children.text: syāayugmake rajau rayau same cejjarau jarau gururyavātparā matīyam // KedV_4.12 //
children.translated_text: In the non-even [quarters], <s>ra</s>-<s>ja</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ra</s>-<s>ya</s> and <s>u</s>; and in the even [quarter], <s>ja</s>-<s>ra</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ja</s>-<s>ra</s> and <s>u</s>, [then] a heavy syllable — this is called <s>yavāt-parā matī</s>. // KedV_4.12 //
Thus ends the fourth chapter on <s>ardhasama</s> (half-equal) meters in the commentary on the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> composed by <s>Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa</s>, son of the illustrious <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmeśvara</s>.
Chapter Five.
[Section on <s>padacaturūrdhva</s> meters (1-5)]
The opening verse (<s>mukhavāda</s>) has eight syllables; the subsequent [verses] increase progressively by the number of syllables in the ocean (i.e., four). //
Is called by those of pure intellect a <s>padacaturūrdhva</s> (four-above-the-foot) meter. // KedV_5.1 //
That [meter] whose beauty is always accomplished through varied feet (<s>pādas</s>),
In the first stated meter, when the odd feet have [a certain] arrangement, //
With light syllables, pauses, feet, extension, and fixed measure — this is <s>pīḍa</s>. // KedV_5.2 //
Ending with a pair of heavy syllables, and containing [the gaṇa] <s>āṅā</s>,
When [the meter] in the first [and] other feet has the distinguishing mark arising from [a different arrangement], /
And if the other [feet] have a different movement, and the fourth [foot as well],
Has a pair of feet [of a certain kind] — that is [called] <s>kalikā</s>. // KedV_5.3 //
Ending with equal feet joined with two heavy syllables, the third [foot] assumes [the pattern] situated in the opening foot; /

children.text: aparamiha lakṣma prakṛtamakhilamapi yadidamanubhavati lavalī sā // KedV_5.4 //
children.translated_text: If the other distinguishing mark here is natural, and [the meter] assumes all of it — that is <s>lavalī</s>. // KedV_5.4 //
If the first [foot] inhabits the fourth [position], with the final foot ending in a pair of heavy syllables, /
And all else above is as stated — then, possessed of graceful feet, this is <s>amṛtadhārā</s>. // KedV_5.5 //
[Section on <s>udgatā</s> meters (6-8)]
In the first [foot] <s>sa</s>-<s>ja</s>, then <s>sa</s> and two light [syllables]; then <s>na</s>-<s>sa</s>-<s>ja</s> with heavy [syllables] — this is <s>udgatā</s>. /

children.text: tryaṅghrigatabhanajalā gayutāḥ sajasā agau caraṇamekataḥ paṭhet // KedV_5.6 //
children.translated_text: In three feet <s>bha</s>-<s>na</s>-<s>ja</s>-<s>la</s> with <s>ga</s> added; <s>sa</s>-<s>ja</s>-<s>sa</s>, <s>a</s> and <s>ga</s> and <s>u</s> — the single [remaining] foot should be recited [separately]. // KedV_5.6 //
When three feet follow the complete distinguishing mark of <s>udgatā</s>, /

children.text: nā bhagau bhavati saurabhakaṃ caraṇe yadīha bhavatastṛtīyake // KedV_5.7 //
children.translated_text: And <s>nā</s>, <s>bha</s>, <s>ga</s> and <s>u</s> occur in the third foot here — [this] becomes <s>saurabhaka</s>. // KedV_5.7 //

children.text: nayugaṃ sakārayugalaṃ ca bhavati caraṇe tṛtīyake /
children.translated_text: When the <s>na</s>-pair and the <s>sa</s>-<s>kāra</s>-pair occur in the third foot, /

children.text: taduditamurumatibhirlalitaṃ yadi śeṣamasya khalu pūrvatulyakam // KedV_5.8 //
children.translated_text: That is declared by those of great intellect to be <s>lalita</s>, if the remainder is indeed equal to the first [pattern]. // KedV_5.8 //
[Section on <s>upasthitapracupita</s> meters (9-11)]

children.text: msau jbhau gau prathamāṅghrirekataḥ pṛthaganyattritayaṃ sanajaragāstato nanau saḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ma</s>-<s>sa</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ja</s>-<s>bha</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>ga</s> and <s>u</s> — the first foot stands alone; the other three separately are <s>sa</s>-<s>na</s>-<s>ja</s>-<s>ra</s>-<s>ga</s>; then <s>na</s>-<s>na</s> and <s>u</s>, <s>sa</s>. /
Adorned with three <s>na</s>-gaṇas and <s>ja</s>-<s>ya</s> — this <s>pracupita</s> is said to be preceded by <s>upasthita</s>. // KedV_5.9 //

children.text: nau pāde 'tha tṛtīyake sanau nasayuktau prathamāṅghrikṛtayatistu vardhamānam /
children.translated_text: <s>Na</s> and <s>u</s> in the foot; then in the third [foot] <s>sa</s>-<s>na</s> and <s>u</s>; <s>na</s>-<s>sa</s> joined — the caesura established in the first foot makes [this] <s>vardhamāna</s>. /

children.text: tritayamaparamapi pūrvasadṛśamiha bhavati pratatamatibhiriti gaditaṃ laghu vṛttam // KedV_5.10 //
children.translated_text: The other three [feet] also are like the first here — this is declared by the learned to be the <s>pratata</s> light meter. // KedV_5.10 //
They call [the meter] with a pause in the first [foot] <s>ārṣabha</s>. //

children.text: tacchuddhavirāṭ puraḥ sthitaṃ tritayamaparamapi yadi pūrvasamaṃ syāt // KedV_5.11 //
children.translated_text: That pure <s>virāṭ</s>, placed first — if the other three [feet] are also equal to the first, [it is <s>ārṣabha</s>]. // KedV_5.11 //
A <s>chandas</s> (meter) with feet of unequal syllables, or with unequal feet, like the <s>daśadharma</s> — /

children.text: yacchando noktamatra gātheti tatsūribhiḥ proktam // KedV_5.12 //
children.translated_text: Whatever meter is not described here, the sages call it <s>gāthā</s>. // KedV_5.12 //
Thus ends the fifth chapter in the commentary on the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> composed by <s>Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa</s>, son of the illustrious <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmeśvara</s>.
Chapter Six.
[<s>Prastāra</s> (Expansion/Tabulation)]
<s>Prastāra</s> (expansion), <s>naṣṭa</s> (lost [meter]), <s>uddiṣṭa</s> (indicated [meter]), <s>ekadvayādilagakriyā</s> (process of one-light, two-light, etc.), /
<s>Saṅkhyāna</s> (enumeration), and <s>adhvayoga</s> (path-calculation) — these six are known as the <s>pratyayas</s> (methods of verification). // KedV_6.1 //
In a foot consisting entirely of heavy syllables, placing a light [syllable] first, below the heavy [syllable]; /

children.text: yathopari tathā śeṣaṃ bhūyaḥ kuryādamuṃ vidhim // KedV_6.2 //
children.translated_text: Making the rest the same as above — one should repeat this procedure. // KedV_6.2 //
Where [syllables are] deficient, one should place heavy [syllables] only, until [the foot becomes] entirely light. /
This <s>prastāra</s> (expansion) has been described by those versed in metrical investigation. // KedV_6.3 //
[<s>Naṣṭa</s> (Finding a Lost Meter)]

children.text: naṣṭasya yo bhavedaṅkastasyārdhe 'rdhe same ca laḥ //
children.translated_text: Of the lost [meter], whatever its serial number may be — if the half of the half is even, [place] a light [syllable]; //
If odd, adding one, in the half of the half there should be a heavy [syllable]. // KedV_6.4 //
[<s>Uddiṣṭa</s> (Identifying a Meter)]
For the indicated [meter], one should write the serial numbers above, starting from twice [the value of] the first; /

children.text: laghusthā ye ca tatrāṅkāstaiḥ saikairmiśritairbhavet // KedV_6.5 //
children.translated_text: Those numbers that stand at [the position of] light [syllables] — with those, increased by one and combined, [the serial number] is obtained. // KedV_6.5 //
[<s>Ekadvayādilagakriyā</s> (Process of Counting Meters with One, Two, etc. Light Syllables)]
The syllables of the meter, increased by one, placed one below the other in descending order, /
Should be placed one above the other successively, starting from one. // KedV_6.6 //
One should stop from the penultimate, dropping one [from the top] each time. /
One from the heavy [syllable] above at the beginning — [this is] the process of counting meters with one, two, etc. light syllables. // KedV_6.7 //
[<s>Saṅkhyāna</s> (Enumeration)]
In the collection of numbers from the light-syllable process, when combined, the count is obtained. /
Or, the sum of the <s>uddiṣṭa</s> numbers, increased by one, may generate this [total]. // KedV_6.8 //
[<s>Adhvayoga</s> (Path-Calculation)]
The count itself, doubled and diminished by one with the [number of] syllables — is declared by the learned to be the <s>adhvan</s> (path). //
The extension of the meter in finger-breadths — one should make finger-breadths below. // KedV_6.9 //
Born in the lineage of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, of manifest virtues and qualities, a knower of <s>Śaiva Siddhānta</s>,
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Pavya</s> (i.e., <s>Parvya</s>), of most pure intellect in comprehending the true meaning of the <s>Vedas</s>; /
<s>Kedāra</s> is his son, with mind single-pointedly devoted to the worship of the feet of <s>Śiva</s>, [who composed] this delightful [work] on <s>chandas</s> (meter)
Called the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> (Ocean of Metrical Gems). // KedV_6.10 //

Thus ends the sixth chapter on <s>prastāra</s> (expansion) in the commentary on the <s>Vṛttaratnākara</s> composed by <s>Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭa</s>, son of the illustrious <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmeśvara</s>. [The work is] complete.
